Holomorphic decompositions of tempered distributions

Written by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. Public domain (CC0).

Every tempered distribution can be recovered by averaging the boundary values of one holomorphic function over a sphere of imaginary directions. The function is uniquely determined by that average. Its individual boundary values can have analytic singularities only in the opposite cotangent direction. We construct this representation by Fourier multipliers, prove the converse from a global growth bound, and localize the directions carried by an arbitrary finite measure on the sphere.

We use the complete proofs in Schwartz functions and Fourier inversion, F1–F5; Lipschitz graphs and surface measures, Theorem 2.1 and its graph density; Holomorphic boundaries in convex cones, the polydisk Cauchy proof; Holomorphic boundaries and analytic directions, Theorem 2; and Cones and derivative-growth wavefronts, the definition, class comparisons, finite-sum and projection arguments. The finite integral Taylor formula is proved in When a kernel is smooth, “Taylor estimates on compact neighborhoods.” The supplied integration foundation, Sections 15.0–15.1 and 16.1–16.2, supplies convergence, product integration and linear changes of variables.

Selecting directions with a measure on the sphere

Let be any finite signed or complex Borel measure on , let be its total variation, and let . Define

The common finite seminorm bound in Theorem 3 proves that this is tempered. A finite complex measure here is equivalently a finite linear combination of finite positive measures; the usual absolute integral bound uses its total variation. No positivity assumption on is needed. Its support is closed, hence compact; the complement has zero total variation, as follows by covering it with the countable basis of zero-measure open sets in the compact metric sphere. Empty support therefore gives the zero measure.
